note: Single-pass extraction by Claude reading the paper text; evidence references sections/figures/tables. No multi-run validation.

components.description: Empirical decline in 'unsupervised' framing -> hypotheses -> risks -> how supervision enters -> proposal

nodes.name: Unlabeled does not mean unsupervised
nodes.description: The absence of human labels does not imply the absence of human supervision, since data curation, preprocessing and learning-objective choices embed substantial human priors.

nodes.name: Dataset curation embeds priors
nodes.description: ImageNet organizes classes around WordNet synsets, and vision-language datasets depend strongly on metadata design and curation choices.

nodes.name: Web-scale data carries regularities
nodes.description: Even without manual curation, common web queries yield regularized patterns such as canonical object poses, centered compositions and consistent orientations, which models inherit.

nodes.name: Contrastive objectives assume object-centricity
nodes.description: Contrastive learning assumes augmented views of one sample depict the same entity and different samples distinct entities; this holds in curated object-centric datasets but not universally, e.g. in multi-entity scenes, textures, microscopy or medical imagery.

nodes.name: DINO degrades with generic data
nodes.description: When training data scale is increased by adding generic non-object-centric images, DINO performance degrades, showing a mismatch between data priors and the learning objective.

nodes.name: Pre-training shifted unsupervised learning from in-domain to cross-domain
nodes.description: Before large-scale pre-training unsupervised learning was predominantly in-domain with explicit, localized assumptions; modern pre-training is adopted across domains so embedded priors become generic and invisible.

nodes.name: Title usage of unsupervised terms declines after 2021
nodes.description: Across CVPR/ICCV/ECCV titles 2013-2025, 'unsupervised' and 'self-supervised' peak around 2021 and then decline despite growing publication counts; at CVPR the 'unsupervised' fraction falls from nearly 4% in 2021 to close to 1% by 2025.

nodes.name: Full-text pre-training reliance follows same pattern
nodes.description: In 17,435 CVPR papers (2015-2025), the share explicitly relying on a named pre-trained model rises from 10.13% in 2015 to 22.17% in 2021 and falls to 15.52% in 2024 and 12.85% in 2025.

nodes.name: Pre-training dependence is concentrated
nodes.description: Among 287 CVPR 2020-2025 papers titled 'unsupervised', reliance on external pre-training rises steadily and is concentrated in a few backbone families (DINO, CLIP, MoCo, diffusion models, SwAV).

nodes.name: Hypotheses for the shift
nodes.description: Three hypotheses may explain the decline: comparison pressure favoring scaled pre-trained models, unsupervised learning becoming an implicit component rather than a stated contribution, and user-side indifference to the training paradigm.

nodes.name: Misattribution of emergent behavior
nodes.description: Properties attributed to an 'unsupervised' method, such as semantic discovery, objectness or robustness, may be inherited from pre-trained representations, so shared upstream priors can be misread as novel emergent principles.

nodes.name: Reduced methodological diversity and barriers
nodes.description: Ambiguity distorts incentives toward adapting to pre-trained models, marginalizes approaches that avoid pre-training or certain priors, and makes same-scale comparison harder for compute-limited researchers.

nodes.name: Erosion of conceptual clarity
nodes.description: Grouping methods with different assumptions under one 'unsupervised' label obscures how a method learns and what it assumes, hindering fair comparison.

nodes.name: Proposal: disclose priors
nodes.description: Authors should disclose priors in data selection and learning objectives and specify which pipeline components depend on which assumptions, via a checklist covering pre-training dependence, frozen vs adaptive reliance, pre-training data scope, data distribution priors, learning invariances and leakage risks.

nodes.name: Proposal: test across pre-training regimes and value relaxation
nodes.description: Methods using pre-trained features should be tested across pre-training regimes, and relaxing assumptions should be valued as a contribution, not only peak benchmark performance.

isolated_nodes.name: Priors are not illegitimate
isolated_nodes.description: Exploiting human priors in data and objectives is often sensible and productive; the paper argues such methods should be described accurately, not avoided.

isolated_nodes.name: Same-scale comparison barrier
isolated_nodes.description: Widely adopted pre-trained models need substantial compute, limiting who can contribute new ideas in GPU-poor academic settings.

structural_reasoning: Empirical venue statistics motivate hypotheses and risks; mechanisms of how supervision enters without labels support the disclosure proposal.
